verses.author: model_A
verses.text: She folds the letter twice before deciding not to send it.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Dust settles on the piano no one plays anymore,
morning light finds the keys anyway.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The kettle clicks off and no one comes—
steam fogs the window
until the garden disappears.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
She counts the coins twice on the counter,
still short for the bus fare home.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A crow lands on the wire, considers something,
then leaves without deciding—
the wire keeps its small, cold hum.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I fold the letter smaller than it needs to be,
small enough to fit in a pocket, or forget.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Someone leaves the porch light burning all night—
not for anyone coming home,
just to keep the moths company.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The kettle clicks off and no one moves—
steam thins into the shape of what we didn't say.
